items.title: CMB.TECH Q3 profit $373.9m; Q4 VLCC spot booked at $635,199/day
items.summary: CMB.TECH reported Q3 2026 profit of $373.9m (EPS $1.29) on revenue of $802.9m, against $17.3m profit a year earlier. Q4-to-date spot TCE is $635,199/day for VLCCs (59% of days fixed) and $377,164/day for Suezmaxes (68% fixed), while its 25k dwt stainless chemical tanker pool earned $18,756/day QTD versus $21,601 in Q3. The company declared $0.65/share and flagged newbuilding deliveries as a headwind, with VLCC fleet growth forecast at 7.1% in 2027 and 16.1% in 2028.

items.title: US sanctions payment networks behind Iran's tanker trade
items.summary: Treasury sanctioned 22 entities and eight individuals on Nov 23 under 'Operation Economic Outcast', aiming at the finance side rather than ships. Targets include Dubai firms said to handle payments for NITC, NIOC oil and petrochemical sales, LPG sales tied to Kharg Petrochemical, and the charter of the tanker SERENE I (IMO 9197832), plus Iran's currency and gold exchange centre.

items.title: US investigating cyberattacks on up to 50 energy tankers
items.summary: Citing the Wall Street Journal, Cornerstone Futures reports the US is looking into cyberattacks on as many as 50 energy tankers, some of which also received bomb threats. Officials reportedly see Iran as the main suspect and Russia as a possibility, but a Trump administration official said no evidence of Iranian involvement has been found; attribution is unconfirmed.

items.title: Brent Dec–Jan spread narrows to $0.16 as Gulf flows hold up
items.summary: Gulf News reports the Brent Dec–Jan spread has fallen to $0.16/bbl from $3.67 in October, with Brent about 24% (roughly $28) below its late-October peak. Middle East flows have proved steadier than the attacks suggest, helped by bypass pipelines and ship-to-ship transfers.

items.title: High tanker and VLGC values prompt quick resales
items.summary: Broker-reported deals cited from Splash247 include Trafigura buying the suezmax Seaways Sabine for about $74m in September and reselling it for about $110m two months later, and MISC reportedly selling the 21-year-old shuttle tanker Jasmine Knutsen, bought for about $33m and now valued near $110m. Sale prices are reported by brokers and not confirmed by the companies.

items.title: Aegean Shipping orders two more LR2s at COSCO Yangzhou
items.summary: Aegean Shipping has added a further pair of LR2 product tanker newbuildings at COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry's Yangzhou yard. Price and delivery dates were not stated in the summary seen.

items.title: Shipping Corp of India tenders for up to 22 newbuilds worth about $3.2bn
items.summary: State-owned SCI is launching tenders for up to 22 newbuildings across gas carriers, tankers and container ships, estimated at $3.2bn, alongside a separate search for secondhand tonnage.

items.title: Hormuz: ten tankers struck in a week; Iran adds 26 tugs to its list
items.summary: UKMTO reported attacks on Nov 22 on three eastbound tankers in Hormuz and a bulk carrier anchored off Khor Fakkan (fire, no casualties), bringing JMIC's count to 10 tankers hit since Nov 16. JMIC logged 114 US-facilitated transits on Nov 19–21 (about 38/day, versus a 2025 average near 138/day), with about 218 ships waiting east of the Strait. The IMO counts 141 incidents and 25 seafarer deaths as of Nov 23; Iran's IRGC separately claims three tankers hit mines, which has not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Swedish Club repeats advice to avoid Hormuz unless essential
items.summary: The Gothenburg-based P&I club told members in a Nov 24 update to avoid Hormuz transits unless operationally essential, and to review war-risk cover, sanctions exposure, navigation capability and crew readiness. Independent monitoring recorded 106 facilitated transits on Nov 15–18, about 26.5 per day.

items.title: Mississippi at New Orleans: safety zone stays through Dec 11
items.summary: After the tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck and capsized the docked cruise vessel American Heritage on Nov 13, the Coast Guard set a safety zone between miles 95.5 and 96.5 of the Lower Mississippi, running through Dec 11. The river is not closed, but the alternate channel is shut and deep-draft vessels and tows of 10 or more barges move one way through the Crescent City Connection main span.

items.title: LA–Long Beach security workers reach tentative labor deal
items.summary: Employers and unionized security workers at Los Angeles and Long Beach reached a tentative agreement extending their contract, pending ratification. The covered terminals handle about 85% of Long Beach cargo and 33% of Los Angeles cargo.

items.title: Container spot rates: Shanghai–LA $7,026/FEU, down 5%
items.summary: For the week to Nov 19, Shanghai–Los Angeles fell 5% to $7,026/FEU and Shanghai–New York fell 9% to $8,194, while Shanghai–Genoa rose 6% to $4,436. Platts put India–US East Coast at $6,275/FEU, 44% below its mid-September peak.

items.title: Monday Nov 23 close: S&P 500 7,237.17 (+4.7%), Nasdaq +6.5%
items.summary: In the latest completed session, the S&P 500 rose 326.78 points (4.7%) to 7,237.17, the Dow rose 1,447.98 (3.0%) to 49,595.31 and the Nasdaq rose 1,471.82 (6.5%) to 24,089.56. The gain recovered just over half of last week's loss and ended a seven-day losing streak for the S&P 500, led by Nvidia after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

items.title: Tuesday midday: Dow +0.8%, S&P 500 −0.5%, Nasdaq −1.4% as chips retreat
items.summary: As of about 1:00 pm ET on Nov 24 (session not yet closed), the Dow was at 49,997.70 (+0.81%), the S&P 500 at 7,202.38 (−0.48%) and the Nasdaq at 23,744.60 (−1.43%). Chipmakers gave back part of Monday's gain, with Nvidia down about 7% after its 31% rise on Monday following Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO.

items.title: Oil: Brent $90.52 (+1.3%), WTI $81.33 (+1.5%) midday Tuesday
items.summary: At 1:03 pm EDT on Nov 24, Brent was up $1.15 at $90.52/bbl and WTI up $1.16 at $81.33, after both touched their lowest levels since August earlier in the session (Brent $88.10, WTI $79.07). Monday's settlements were Brent $89.37 (−3.46%) and WTI $80.17 (−3.88%). New ship attacks near Hormuz supported prices, while Deutsche Bank's estimate of a 1.7 million b/d surplus limited gains.

items.title: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $175/share, about $41.0bn
items.summary: Sanofi will acquire Insmed for $175 per share in cash, an equity value of about $41.0bn (€37.6bn), funded with debt and cash. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to Insmed shareholder and regulatory approvals; Sanofi expects the deal to add to EPS by the end of 2028.

items.title: 10-year yield 4.92%; markets price ~98% odds of Dec 9 Fed hike
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield ended Nov 23 at 4.92% and the 2-year at 4.63%, both unchanged, while the 30-year eased about 2 bp to 5.29%. CME FedWatch showed about 98% odds of a 25 bp rate increase at the Dec 9 meeting. Figures come from an AI-assisted recap that cites CNBC, AP and Bloomberg. Midday Nov 24, Yahoo Finance showed the 10-year near 4.90% and futures pricing about a 95% chance of a 25 bp hike.

items.title: Dollar index +0.5% to 104.35; gold +3.4%, US natural gas $3.536
items.summary: On Nov 23 the dollar index rose 0.52% to about 104.35, EUR/USD fell 0.60% to 1.0904 and USD/JPY rose to about 158.94. Gold futures gained 3.38% to $3,634.30/oz and Henry Hub natural gas rose 3.66% to $3.536/MMBtu.

items.title: Holiday week: GDP and PCE data Wednesday; markets shut Thursday
items.summary: GDP and PCE inflation figures are due Wednesday, Nov 25, at 7:30 am CT. US stock markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early, at noon CT, on Friday.

items.title: Iran says no talks with US until its seven conditions are met
items.summary: Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf said Tehran will not negotiate until its conditions are met; state media say they include lifting sanctions, ending the US naval blockade of Iranian ports and releasing seized assets, though Iran has not published the list. Separately, US Vice President Vance and Secretary of State Rubio met Qatar's prime minister at the White House.

items.title: Trump says he may renew Iran strikes after New Year without a deal
items.summary: Trump said he is inclined to resume strikes on Iran after the New Year unless Tehran agrees to a long-term deal on hostilities and nuclear limits. Separately, Iran's deputy foreign minister said Iran would take whatever measures it considers necessary.

items.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill at least 9, including Hamas security official
items.summary: AP reported at least nine Palestinians killed in four Israeli strikes overnight Monday into Tuesday, among them Na'im Abu Nahl, head of internal security at the Hamas-run Interior Ministry. Gaza's health ministry puts the war's death toll at 74,746.

items.title: Ukrainian strike halts Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Rostov
items.summary: A Ukrainian missile and drone attack stopped operations at the Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Russia's Rostov region, according to the regional governor. Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence indicates Russia is preparing new large-scale strikes. A Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia killed two people and wounded 40, Just Security's daily summary reports.
items.source: The Standard / Everything Briefing / Just Security

items.title: EU proposes 22nd Russia sanctions package
items.summary: The European Commission unveiled its 22nd sanctions package against Russia on Nov 23. Reported measures include a ban on Russian athletes competing under the Russian flag in the EU and a visa ban on Russian ex-combatants.

items.title: Estonia to close its border with Russia
items.summary: Estonia plans to close its border with Russia after Moscow accused it of hostile actions, according to Reuters and NBC reports linked in the briefing. Details on timing were not given in the summary seen.

items.title: Indonesia factory fire kills 24, dozens missing
items.summary: Indonesian authorities said 24 people were killed in a factory fire, with dozens still missing, according to a Reuters report linked in the briefing.

items.title: Broncos beat Raiders 38–24, now 8–2; at Steelers Friday 7:00 pm CT
items.summary: Denver beat Las Vegas 38–24 at Empower Field on Nov 22 to move to 8–2, level with Kansas City (8–2) at the top of the AFC West and listed first. Next: at Pittsburgh (6–4) on Friday, Nov 27, at Acrisure Stadium, 7:00 pm Central, on Amazon.

items.title: Texans 4–6 after 26–3 win over Colts; host Ravens Sunday
items.summary: Houston beat Indianapolis 26–3 on Nov 19 to reach 4–6 and sat second in the AFC South behind Jacksonville in ESPN's standings after that game. Defensive end Chris Braswell was carted off with a right knee injury. Next: vs Baltimore at home on Sunday, Nov 29 (schedule lists noon Central, subject to flex changes). ESPN's game page lists Baltimore at 4–7, with quarterback Lamar Jackson on injured reserve (thumb).

items.title: Davis Cup: Machac puts Czechia 1–0 up on Canada
items.summary: In the Final 8 quarterfinal in Bologna on Nov 24, Tomas Machac (No. 59) beat Liam Draxl (No. 154) 6–2, 3–6, 6–2. Jiri Lehecka (No. 14) faces Felix Auger-Aliassime (No. 17) next, with a deciding doubles if needed. Italy plays South Korea Wednesday; Germany–Great Britain and Austria–Spain follow Thursday, and the final is Sunday, Nov 29.
items.source: The Canadian Press via paNOW / Tennis TourTalk
